command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
cd /tmp

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e and `set -uo pipefail` does NOT clear it
# (spawn#707), so errexit is off above and every status is checked by hand.

IDX=mpa_vJun23_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202403
MD5=8caae86b4d2931416cbdbb92f5985cef
HOST=https://cmprod1.cibio.unitn.it/biobakery4/metaphlan_databases/bowtie2_indexes

echo "== /tmp is a tmpfs at HALF the instance RAM, so check the room BEFORE a 23 GB fetch =="
df -BG /tmp | awk 'NR==2{print "  tmpfs\t"$2" total, "$4" free"}'
FREE=$(df -BG /tmp | awk 'NR==2{gsub(/G/,"",$4); print $4}')
test "$FREE" -ge 26 || { echo "only ${FREE}G free in /tmp; a 23 GB index needs more"; exit 1; }

echo "== fetch the DEPOSITORS prebuilt bowtie2 index =="
# NOT built here on purpose. MetaPhlAn publishes this index with its own md5, and it is
# byte-identical to what `metaphlan --install` fetches -- so the bytes are checkable AT
# THE SOURCE. A locally built index would be unverifiable against anything, and
# bowtie2-build over the full CHOCOPhlAn marker set is hours of CPU for a worse artifact.
T0=$(date +%s)
curl -fL --no-progress-meter --retry 3 --retry-delay 10 -o "${IDX}_bt2.tar" "$HOST/${IDX}_bt2.tar"
RC=$?; T1=$(date +%s)
echo "fetch_rc\t$RC"
test "$RC" = "0" || { echo "download failed"; exit 1; }
BYTES=$(stat -c%s "${IDX}_bt2.tar")
echo "download_s\t$(( T1 - T0 ))"
echo "bytes\t$BYTES"
awk -v b=$BYTES -v s=$((T1-T0)) 'BEGIN{if(s>0)printf "MB_per_s\t%.1f\n", b/1e6/s}'

echo "== verify against the published md5 =="
echo "$MD5  ${IDX}_bt2.tar" > want.md5
md5sum -c want.md5 || { echo "published md5 MISMATCH -- do not stage these bytes"; exit 1; }
echo "md5\tmatches the published $MD5"

echo "== our pin on the staged copy =="
sha256sum "${IDX}_bt2.tar" | tee "${IDX}_bt2.tar.sha256"

echo "== what is inside (listing only; untarring would need a second 23 GB) =="
tar -tf "${IDX}_bt2.tar" | head -10
N=$(tar -tf "${IDX}_bt2.tar" | wc -l)
echo "entries\t$N"
# bowtie2 LARGE index: .1.bt2l .2.bt2l .3.bt2l .4.bt2l .rev.1.bt2l .rev.2.bt2l
BT2=$(tar -tf "${IDX}_bt2.tar" | grep -c "bt2l$")
echo "bt2l_files\t$BT2"
test "$BT2" -ge 6 || { echo "expected >=6 .bt2l files, found $BT2"; exit 1; }
echo "STAGE OK"
